column7: A highly tweakable octave fuzz with separate clean and fuzz outputs, Low and High EQ controls, Fuzz Volume, Clean Volume, Gain and Chaos. Contemporary 2023 coverage describes Chaos as progressively adding intermodulation and upper-octave content; it is a distinct product from Rabbit Hole FX's earlier Merkin.
column10: The clean-blend architecture, dual-channel volume controls and Chaos control are strong external identifiers. Do not merge it with the older Merkin despite shared design lineage.

column7: Two-knob CMOS fuzz using a 4069 device to transform guitar signal into a square-wave texture. Volume controls output and Sensitivity controls input gain/behavior, ranging from sputter and sub-octave hints toward self-oscillation. Contemporary coverage dates the unveiling to September 2023.
column10: The unusually simple two-knob layout, 4069 CMOS basis and glitch/self-oscillation behavior make this easy to identify from the enclosure and controls. Preserve it separately from later Hungry Robot fuzzes.

column7: German-made Octavia revision documented in 2023 with Schottky-based octave/fuzz design, custom transformer, silent switching and the added Edge control. The V2 separates from the earlier V1 through its control and component-generation markers.
column10: V2 is retained as the marketed generation label because 2023 coverage explicitly uses it. Edge control, MagTrAB silent switching and Schottky/custom-transformer description are high-value identifiers.

column7: Hand-wired Custom Shop fuzz developed around late-1960s British fuzz inspiration, with expanded gain and filtering. MKII moved the product into a smaller board-friendly enclosure while retaining hand-wired construction and adding Thick, curated three-position Filter and internal Bias controls.
column10: Preserve original Custom Filter Fuzz and MKII as separate production identities. The enclosure transition and documented filter/bias control set are useful specimen-level clues.

column7: Fuzz and analog MS-20-style filter combination derived from the Singularity fuzz section of Black Hole Symmetry. Gain, Master, cutoff, Resonance, LPF Volume, 2-pole/4-pole, Add Fuzz, serial/parallel routing and expression/CV create a distinctive guitar-synth hybrid identity. Made in France.
column10: The MS-20-style filter, cutoff fader, serial/parallel routing and CV/expression input distinguish TARS sharply from conventional fuzzes and from the Black Hole Symmetry source family.

column7: Sutton Instruments' first pedal, a 1970s-inspired extended-range fuzz with independent boost. Fuzz controls include Sustain, Presence, Tone, Volume and Heavy/Light clipping, while the separate boost provides additional level. Contemporary coverage places the launch in February 2023; the builder currently continues to list the product.
column10: The independent boost, extended-range fuzz controls and Heavy/Light clipping selector are strong identification markers. Preserve the later bass version as a related but separate product identity.
